Instead, most of the costs were estimated using a scaling approach. This entailed scaling cost estimates from previous NETL studies according to the methodology presented in the 2024 revision of the QGESS document “Capital Cost Scaling Methodology: Revision 4b Report” (NETL, 2025a). For most process equipment, Equation 2-1 is used to scale costs. Equation 2-1. EXP SP SC = RC∗� � where: RP EXP – exponent RC – reference cost RP – reference parameter SC – scaled cost SP – scaling parameter If the scaling algorithm for a piece of process equipment did not exist in the QGESS, an appropriate scaling parameter was selected using best engineering judgement and a scaling exponent of 0.6 was selected per the “rule of six-tenths” (Anderson, 2009). Most process equipment capital costs were scaled from natural gas study cases of a previous NETL hydrogen study (Lewis, et al., 2022). The CO capture systems were scaled from quotes obtained directly 2 from Shell, the vendor that developed these technologies used in this study. Costs for select process equipment, including the air compressor, secondary reformer, ammonia production system, and methanation unit, were obtained from Black & Veatch, an EPC company. The goal of engaging B&V was to obtain recent estimates to replace legacy cost data or to provide new costs for equipment that did not have an analogous cost reference from previous NETL studies. 2.11.1.2 System Code-of-Accounts The costs are grouped according to a process/system-oriented code of accounts. This type of code-of-account structure has the advantage of grouping all reasonably allocable components of a system or process so that they are included in the specific system account. This would not be the case had a facility, area, or commodity account structure been chosen instead. 2.11.1.3 Estimate Scope The estimates represent a complete ammonia production facility on a generic site. The plant boundary limit is defined as the total plant facility within the “fence line” including feedstock receiving and water supply system but terminating at the injection point into an ammonia storage tank. Ammonia storage and transport is beyond the estimate scope. CO T&S cost is not 2 included in the reported capital cost or O&M costs but is treated separately and added to the LCOA. 37 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION 2.11.1.4 Capital Cost Assumptions The following assumptions are reflected in the costs scaled according to NETL QGESS methodology: • Labor costs are based on Midwest, Merit Shop. Costs curated by B&V are based on a U.S. Gulf Coast location and the labor cost has been factored to a Midwest location. Labor cost data were sourced from recent projects and proprietary B&V in-house references/cost databases. • The estimates are based on a competitive bidding environment, with adequate skilled craft labor available locally. • Labor is based on a 50-hour work week (5 days x 10 hours).
